_notes: Taito do Brasil Oba-Oba (1980) on the later hardware: the 1979 firmware moved up to the 0x4000 window. It keeps
the 1979 structure - credits display at 0x408F, player count at 0x408D - but puts settings, high score and stored
credits where the 1981-85 boards do (0x4070, 0x4079, 0x407F). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the ROM code and
a live obaoba capture on an AtGames ALP4K (Visual Pinball Standalone): a full one-player game read back its final
score of 16,312 (held in 0x40F4 afterwards) and two credits, with 0x408D at 1 and 0x408F at 2 throughout, current
player 1 during play and 0 in attract, and the games-played counter ticking at game start. The game was tilted
on ball 5, which set bit 1 of the flags byte. obaoba1 - ROM code references every declared address identically.
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); balls per game is its first byte and the three replay levels its fifth to seventh.
No checksum. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset; PinMAME's taito driver (2026-10)
marks the saved game over on load so a table starts in attract.
0x40F4-0x40FF holds the last game's final display (four scores, same encoding as 0x4080) once the game is over, while the attract alternates the live display between it and the high score.

player_count._notes: 1979-style position; 1 throughout a live one-player game, 0 in attract. The reset path refuses to resume with 5 or more here.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: 0 in attract, 1 during a one-player game (live).
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x408F (1979-style), 2 in both during the live game.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser). Reads 0xFF in attract before any game on this firmware.
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

tilted._notes: Bit 1 of the flags byte. Pulsed briefly once mid-ball with scoring continuing (the tilt warning), then set and held from the real tilt on ball 5 until the game ended (live).
tilted.label: Tilted

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

02.label: Replay Level 1
02._notes: One BCD byte compared against the two most-significant digits of the score (x10,000). A level equal to the one before it is skipped, so 30 30 30 is a single replay at 300,000. The same routine in every set.

01._notes: Ticked at game start in the live capture. BCD per the firmware's ADD M / DAA increment; only values below 10 have been seen.
01.label: Games Played
